Dissection puzzle (Perigal or Bhaskara) with paper squares.

Goal: I can prove the Pythagorean Theorem by rearranging areas.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Pythagorean Theorem: in a right triangle with legs a and b and hypotenuse c, a2 + b2 = c2.

Proof by area: arrange four copies of the right triangle inside a square of side a + b, leaving a tilted square of side c in the middle. The big square's area is (a + b)2 = a2 + 2ab + b2. It is also four triangles plus the middle square: 4 times (1/2)ab + c2 = 2ab + c2. Set them equal and subtract 2ab: a2 + b2 = c2.
